summary: Jayandra Soni is a scholar in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He earned Ph.D.s from Banaras Hindu University (~1975–1978) and McMaster University (~1982–1987), and served as a lecturer at the University of Marburg (~1991–2012).

Jaś Elsner works in the fields of religious studies and history and archaeology. He has held academic posts at the University of Michigan and the University of Chicago (~2013), and he taught Sun-Ah Choi.
Jean Dantinne is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Étienne Lamotte. He held a post as a librarian at the University of Liège.

Jean Filliozat was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at INALCO (~1931–1935). He was a professor at the Collège de France (1951–1978) and director of the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1956–1977).

Jean Philippe Vogel was an Indology and archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Amsterdam (~1890–1897). He worked for the Archaeological Survey of India (1910–1911) and served as director at Leiden University (attested 1910, 1914–1939).

Jean Przyluski studied at the EPHE (~1913–1923), working in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He founded Bibliographie bouddhique and held posts at INALCO (1923), the EPHE (~1927–1930), and the Collège de France (~1930–1944).

Jean-Baptiste Biot studied at Collège Louis-le-Grand, École polytechnique, and École Nationale des Ponts et Chaussées. He worked in sinology and history/archaeology, holding posts in the French Revolutionary Army, Bureau des Longitudes, Collège de France, and Science Faculty of Paris.

Jean-François Jarrige was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at Lycée Claude Fauriel and the École du Louvre (~1961–1964). He served as the head of the Musée Guimet from approximately 1986 to 2008.

Jean-Louis Burnouf studied at Collège d'Harcourt and under Antoine-Léonard de Chézy. A linguist, he held posts at Lycée Louis-le-Grand, University of Paris, Collège de France (1817–1844), and École Normale Supérieure (~1826–1844).
Jean-Luc Achard is a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and holds a post at the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique.

Jean-Luc Chevillard is a scholar in the fields of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure in 1975 and served as a researcher at the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique (~1989).

Jean-Noël Robert studied at INALCO, ENLOV, and under Bernard Frank in Japanology, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1990–2011) and the Collège de France (2011–2022).

Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat was a sinologist and linguist who studied at INALCO. He held a professorship in Chinese at the Collège de France from 1815 to 1832, and taught scholars including Stanislas Julien and Eugène Burnouf.

Jeannine Auboyer worked in history, archaeology, and Indology, studying at Académie Julian, École du Louvre (1929–1934), and the EPHE (~1931–1935). She held positions at the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique and the Musée Guimet (1965–1980).
Jeff Dolven studied at Worcester College (~1988–1990) and Yale University (~1990–1997). He founded Princeton University and held a post there around 2001, where he taught Thomas James Mazanec.
Jeff Malpas is a philosopher who taught Sonam Thakchoe and Justin Shimeld. He held a professorship at the University of Tasmania (~1999) and a post at La Trobe University in 2019.

Jeff Wilson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who earned his PhD from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. He studied under mentor Taitetsu Unno and postdoctoral mentor Myōsei Tatsuguchi, and taught Phramonchai Saitanaporn.

Jeffery D. Long is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Chicago (~1993–2000). He became an Associate Professor of Religion and Asian Studies at Elizabethtown College (~2000).

Jeffrey Clark Ruff studied at Missouri State University and UCSB (PhD 2002) under David Gordon White. An Indology and religious studies scholar, his posts include UCSB, University of California (director 2001–2002), and Marshall University (assistant professor 2002).

Jeffrey Davis Schoening is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Washington in 1991, studying under advisor Sanghasen Singh and doctoral supervisor Collett Cox.
